blocks.text: Condo buildings in Cultus Lake East
Cultus Lake East is FVRD Electoral Area H plus Cultus Lake Park Board lease land — it is NOT inside the City of Chilliwack, whatever mailing addresses say.
Streets, schools and getting around Cultus Lake East

items.t: No official boundary for Cultus Lake East is published by the Cultus Lake Park Board, the FVRD or BC Parks. The Cultus Lake Park Plan, Bylaw No. 1080, 2016, designates the residential lots on the east side of the lake and the Mountainview Road and Park Drive areas as Residential, and BC Parks states Columbia Valley Highway bisects the southeast section of Cultus Lake Provincial Park.

Where condo stock concentrates: it does not exist on the east shore. Most of the east shore is Cultus Lake Provincial Park (Entrance Bay, Clear Creek, Delta Grove and Maple Bay campgrounds; Entrance Bay and Maple Bay day-use areas); the private housing is the Park lease-lot strip on Lakeshore Drive and Munroe Avenue (R-3 Waterfront Residential and R-4 Hillside Residential zones in FVRD Cultus Lake Park Zoning Bylaw No. 1375, 2016) plus one manufactured-home park on Columbia Valley Highway. No condo building or townhome complex on the east side was named with a street address on any source checked.
Tenure (the defining fact): east-side homes inside Cultus Lake Park are on leased lots under the Cultus Lake Park Board — leasehold, not freehold.

SD33 catchments are address-based; the sample address 3499 Columbia Valley Hwy was run in the SD33 School Locator and returned no result, because the locator's listed ranges for the road do not include that number — address-level catchment for an east-shore address is not verified. Area-level feeder pattern only (SD33 Administrative Procedure 611): Cultus Lake Elementary School → Mount Slesse Middle School → G.W.

Transit and shopping: BC Transit route 56 Cultus Lake runs along Columbia Valley Highway on the east-shore side, seasonal — summer only, with no year-round service. No shopping centre or grocery store on the east shore is confirmed; the nearest grocery identified in the verified research is Save-on-Foods Sardis, 6014 Vedder Road, Sardis, and the nearest library is Sardis Library, 5819 Tyson Road, Chilliwack.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Cultus Lake East

items.t: Governing zoning and plans (FVRD / Park Board — never Chilliwack's bylaws): FVRD Cultus Lake Park Zoning Bylaw No. 1375, 2016 zones the Park lease lands (R-3 Waterfront Residential and R-4 Hillside Residential on the Lakeshore Drive / Munroe Avenue side; in R-3 the permitted primary uses are a single-detached dwelling or a manufactured home, one per lot; Amendment Bylaw No. 1672 added R-5 Lower Lakeshore Drive and R-6 Upper Lakeshore Drive and amended R-4 height; minimum lot area/frontage for R-3/R-4: Not verified). PlanCultus, Cultus Lake Park Plan Bylaw No. 1080, 2016, covers the Park including the east-side lots; the FVRD Official Community Plan for Electoral Areas E and H, Bylaw No. 1115, covers Area H land outside the Park.

Taxes — rural regime, not Chilliwack's dates: Park lease lots pay Park Board lease charges rather than a standard municipal tax bill (current schedule not verified). For non-Park Electoral Area H land, taxes are provincial rural taxes under the Taxation (Rural Area) Act s. 11: due July 2, with a 5% penalty on amounts unpaid after July 2 and a further 5% on amounts unpaid after October 31. Chilliwack's penalty dates NEVER apply to Cultus Lake.

Manufactured-home park tenancy: site tenancies are governed by BC's Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act — the tenant owns the home and rents the site under a written agreement. The Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Regulation (B.C. Reg. 481/2003) expressly recognises a park reserved for tenants who have reached 55 and allows a landlord to refuse an assignment where the proposed purchaser does not meet the park's age requirement — which is why Cultus Lake Village's own written rule, not a listing label, decides who can buy in. Pad-rent increase limits: 2026 = 2.3% plus a proportional amount for changes in local government levies and regulated utility fees; 2027 = 2.2% plus proportional; 3 full months' written notice, once every 12 months.

blocks.text: Good to know about Cultus Lake East

items.t: Most of the "east shore" is a provincial park, not a housing market. Cultus Lake Provincial Park occupies most of the east shore; the private housing is the Park lease-lot strip on Lakeshore Drive/Munroe Avenue plus one manufactured-home park on the highway. A buyer searching "Cultus Lake East condos" is searching a sub-area with no condo stock at all.

The same park home was marketed as both 45+ and 55+ within one listing cycle. Home 28 at Cultus Lake Village was listed in spring 2026 as a "45+ age park" and later with the park described as a "55+ age park", in otherwise near-identical text. A 45+ label could never be a valid BC strata bylaw — but this is a manufactured-home park, where the age rule is the park's own under tenancy regulation, so only the park's written rules settle it.
There are no SnapStats numbers for anywhere at Cultus Lake.
The school locator literally has gaps on this road.

Sewer at the lake is an area-by-area build-out. The FVRD operates a sewer system for Cultus Lake in Electoral Area H and publishes a Cultus Lake Service Area Map; lots outside a sewer service area use private septic systems regulated by the Fraser Health Authority — connection status is a per-lot check on the east shore too.

A Chilliwack mailing address does not make this Chilliwack. Governance, zoning, plans and taxes here run through the Cultus Lake Park Board and the FVRD (Electoral Area H) — Park Plan Bylaw No. 1080, 2016, Park Zoning Bylaw No. 1375, 2016, and the rural tax regime — not through the City of Chilliwack.

The north end of Cultus Lake is FVRD Electoral Area H plus Cultus Lake Park, governed by the Cultus Lake Park Board — it is NOT inside the City of Chilliwack, whatever mailing addresses say. Lakeside at Cultus Lake is filed in full HERE — it is the lake's only condo-form building, and the 55+ pass checked it and found it NOT 55+.
Lakeside at Cultus Lake — 3175 Columbia Valley Highway (north end)

A waterfront condominium building of 21 homes, developed by Alture Properties with Jim Young on freehold waterfront land (developer source); the developer calls it "a collection of 21 condominium homes" just inside the boundary of the provincial park, each home with a private deck, a boat slip and two parking stalls. Listing data records the building as Apartment/Condo type, built 2019, in board Area Minor "Cultus Lake North"; the building's own site states only 5 of its 21 homes remain, with a private dock and a boat slip for each home. Tenure/form for condo purposes, verified fresh: a freehold strata-form condominium building — NOT Park Board leasehold, NOT bare-land strata, NOT a pad product. Strata plan number: Not confirmed from the sources opened. Published restrictions: listing data in the 55+ pass records pets allowed with restrictions (cats and dogs, two maximum) and no age restriction in any source checked — it is a general-market recreational condominium, verified NOT 55+. No source opened states a rental restriction; in any case a strata rental-restriction bylaw would be VOID since November 24, 2022. (55+ notes

items.t: No official MLS boundary for Cultus Lake North is published by the Park Board or the FVRD. The Park Board states Cultus Lake Park covers 640 acres at the north end of the lake, with the Village Centre site immediately south of Columbia Valley Highway at Sunnyside Boulevard. "Cultus Lake North" is used by the FVRD as a community location name in its Area H Evacuation Guide; it is not a municipal neighbourhood name.

Where condo stock concentrates: in exactly one building. The north end's housing is otherwise single-detached homes and cabins on Park Board leased lots along Sunnyside Boulevard and the Park's residential streets; the one condominium, Lakeside at Cultus Lake, stands at 3175 Columbia Valley Highway at the lake's north end, on freehold waterfront land outside the Park lease system (developer source). Townhome complexes in Cultus Lake North: none confirmed.

Tenure (the defining contrast inside one sub-area): homes inside Cultus Lake Park sit on leased lots administered by the Cultus Lake Park Board under the Cultus Lake Park Act — leasehold, not freehold. Lakeside is the exception: the developer describes freehold waterfront land.

For that sample address, the SD33 School Locator returns Cultus Lake Swílhcha Community School (elementary), Mount Slesse Middle (with the locator note that Mount Slesse students must attend G.W. Graham Secondary), and G.W. Graham Secondary. Catchments for other addresses are not verified — run the exact address.

Village, transit and shopping: Main Beach is the Park Board's main public beach at the north end; Sunnyside Campground, 4165 Columbia Valley Highway, is 65 acres with seasonal, full hook-up and tenting sites, a boat launch and playgrounds; Cultus Lake Community Hall is at 4220 Columbia Valley Highway. The Village Centre / plaza at Columbia Valley Highway and Sunnyside Boulevard is the Park commercial area designated in PlanCultus, and a Park Board committee agenda names Cultus Lake Superette as its grocery and convenience store (street address not verified). BC Transit route 56 runs between Chilliwack (Cottonwood Mall / Promontory area) and the Cultus Lake Marina stop via Vedder Road and Columbia Valley Highway — seasonal, summer months only, no year-round service.

items.t: Taxes — lease charges and the rural regime, not Chilliwack's dates: Park lease lots pay Park Board lease charges rather than a standard municipal tax bill (current schedule and per-lot FVRD levies not verified). For non-Park Electoral Area H land — the frame for a freehold parcel like Lakeside's — taxes are provincial rural taxes under the Taxation (Rural Area) Act s. 11: due July 2, with a 5% penalty on amounts unpaid after July 2 and a further 5% on amounts unpaid after October 31, plus FVRD service-area levies where the lot participates. Chilliwack's penalty dates NEVER apply to Cultus Lake.

blocks.text: Good to know about Cultus Lake North

items.t: The north end's only condominium markets itself on scarcity, not age. Lakeside's own site states only 5 of its 21 homes remain, with a private dock and a boat slip for each home — a recreational product aimed at weekend and second-home buyers, with no age restriction anywhere in its material. Do not let a "Cultus Lake condos" search imply a condo market here: it is one 21-home building.

The Park is self-funded, which is why the lease charges matter. Park Board community material records that Cultus Lake Park receives no local, provincial or federal funding and is entirely self-sustaining, with more than 1,500 residential leaseholders — lease charges are the Park's operating revenue, not a tax bill by another name. That frame does not apply to Lakeside's freehold parcel, which is why the tenure check comes first.

The lake's sewage servicing is being rebuilt in stages, north side first. The FVRD's North Cultus wastewater treatment plant was commissioned in April 2025 under the FVRD Liquid Waste Management Plan (approved 2019), for Class A effluent plus phosphorus removal — 2025 was its first operational year, and it serves the lake's north side. Whether a specific north-end lot is connected is a per-lot check.

"Cultus Lake North" is an emergency-planning name as much as a real estate one. The FVRD uses "Cultus Lake North" as a community location name in its Area H Evacuation Guide; it is not a municipal neighbourhood name, and no official MLS boundary for it is published by the Park Board or the FVRD.

The Village Centre is a negotiation, not a presale. Village Centre redevelopment is a Park Board request-for-proposals process with a preferred proponent in negotiations. A buyer told a new condo project is "coming" at the Village Centre is being told about an RFP — no developer, no disclosure statement, no units.

blocks.text: Condo buildings in Cultus Lake South

The south end of Cultus Lake, including Lindell Beach on the south shore, is FVRD Electoral Area H — OUTSIDE the Cultus Lake Park Board lease lands and NOT inside the City of Chilliwack, whatever mailing addresses say. The three Lindell Beach communities (Creekside Mills, The Cottages at Cultus Lake, Aquadel Crossing) are filed in full HERE, classified by their actual sourced tenure — all three are bare-land strata single-family/cottage communities, not apartment condos. All three were checked in the 55+ pass and are NOT 55+.
Streets, schools and getting around Cultus Lake South

items.t: No official MLS boundary for Cultus Lake South is published by the FVRD or the Park Board. The FVRD lists Lindell Beach, Columbia Valley and Cultus Lake as the communities of Electoral Area H, and also uses "Cultus Lake South" as a community name — it publishes a Cultus Lake South Community Emergency Preparedness Guide.

Where condo stock concentrates: there is no apartment-condo stock at the south end. The attached/stratified stock clusters along Columbia Valley Road at Lindell Beach as bare-land strata single-family communities: Creekside Mills (1687 Columbia Valley Rd, developer source), The Cottages at Cultus Lake (1777 Columbia Valley Rd) and Aquadel Crossing (1885 Columbia Valley Rd, developer source), with the Lindell Beach Holiday Resort at 1920 Columbia Valley Rd. Columbia Valley Road provides one-way-in, one-way-out access, north to the Sardis and Yarrow exits of Highway 1.

Tenure (the defining contrast): unlike the north and east shores, south-end homes are outside the Cultus Lake Park leasehold system — tenure here is freehold lots plus bare land strata, under the FVRD Official Community Plan for Electoral Areas E and H, Bylaw No. 1115; PlanCultus (Bylaw No. 1080, 2016) applies only inside Cultus Lake Park at the north end. Under the OCP designations the only residential use permitted is single family residential use, with housing needs met mainly through infill in existing hamlets.

No sample address was run for this sub-area, so the address-level catchment for south-end addresses is not verified. Area-level feeder pattern only (SD33 Administrative Procedure 611): Cultus Lake Elementary School → Mount Slesse Middle School → G.W. Graham Secondary School.

Transit, shopping and services: BC Transit route 56 ends at the Cultus Lake Marina stop at the north end and does NOT extend to Lindell Beach; service to the lake is seasonal, summer only. No shopping centre or grocery store at the south end is confirmed; the nearest grocery identified in the verified research is Save-on-Foods Sardis, 6014 Vedder Road, Sardis, and the nearest library is Sardis Library, 5819 Tyson Road, Chilliwack. The FVRD operates a sewer system for Cultus Lake in Electoral Area H and publishes a service area map; lots outside a sewer service area use private septic systems regulated by the Fraser Health Authority.

items.t: Governing zoning and OCP (FVRD — never Chilliwack's bylaws, and never the Park Board's): the FVRD Official Community Plan for Electoral Areas E and H, Bylaw No. 1115 (titled "Columbia Valley, Lindell Beach and Chilliwack River Valley," as amended by Bylaw No. 1533, 2019), covers the south end; zoning is in the FVRD Consolidated Zoning Bylaw No. 1638, 2021 — the zone names and minimum parcel area/frontage figures applying to Lindell Beach parcels are not verified and must be checked per address. PlanCultus (Bylaw No. 1080, 2016) does NOT apply here — it applies only inside Cultus Lake Park at the north end.

Taxes — rural regime, not Chilliwack's dates: Electoral Area H properties pay FVRD and provincial rural taxes plus service-area levies. Under the Taxation (Rural Area) Act s. 11, rural taxes are due July 2, with a 5% penalty on amounts unpaid after July 2 and a further 5% on amounts unpaid after October 31. Chilliwack's penalty dates NEVER apply to Cultus Lake. Service detail: the South Cultus Lake sewer service area was established by Bylaw No. 1416, 2017, with a parcel tax under Bylaw No. 1497, 2018; Amendment Bylaw No. 1779, 2025 set the per-parcel amount as the annual requisition divided equally by parcels on the roll; the FVRD's Area H residential rates list Water – Cultus Lake and Sewer – Cultus Lake South as "No Utility Billing / Property Taxes: Yes" (tax-funded) — confirm the specific lot is a participant. Area H - Residential Rates 2026.pdf

Manufactured-home / pad product: where pad product is discussed (Lindell Beach Holiday Resort), tenancies sit under BC's Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act frame and pad-rent increase limits apply: 2026 = 2.3% plus a proportional amount for changes in local government levies and regulated utility fees; 2027 = 2.2% plus proportional. The Holiday Resort's own current terms are not verified — never publish a pad-rent dollar figure for it.

blocks.text: Good to know about Cultus Lake South

items.t: The south end's sewer tax is shared equally, not metered. Amendment Bylaw No. 1779, 2025 set the South Cultus Lake sewer parcel tax as the annual requisition divided equally by the parcels on the roll — every participating parcel pays the same amount regardless of use, and the FVRD's Area H rates show the south sewer and the Cultus Lake water service as tax-funded with no separate utility bill (the north sewer, by contrast, carries a flat rate plus taxes). Area H - Residential Rates 2026.pdf

"Bare land strata" is the whole story at Lindell Beach. All three named communities sell a detached house or cottage, but the title is a bare land strata lot: strata fees, bylaws, a depreciation report and a CRF stand behind the cottage, and the Form B — not the cottage's appearance — is where a buyer learns what the strata maintains and what the lot owner does.

The local hazards are creek fans, not the Fraser River. The governing local hazards at Lindell Beach are lake-level and creek (Frosst Creek) debris/flood events on the Cultus Lake alluvial fans; the FVRD funds sediment-basin cleanouts at Frosst Creek and Elbow Creek in this area, and its Area H guide lists flooding, landslide and slope stability, interface fire, debris slides and flash flooding. Property-specific hazard reports are not verified.
There are no SnapStats numbers for anywhere at Cultus Lake. Lindell Beach is a CADREB board sub-area under the Cultus Lake MLS area, not an FVREB reporting row.

Soowahlie First Nation (IR 14) is at the south end of the lake. The PlanCultus plan map shows Soowahlie First Nation (IR 14) at the south end — a neighbouring jurisdiction a south-end buyer will see on maps and in addressing, distinct from both the Park and the FVRD lots.

The Holiday Resort's tenure is documented by a court, not a brochure. The only hard source on the Lindell Beach Holiday Resort's model is the BC Court of Appeal's 2009 record (owned pre-fabricated trailer on a leased pad; 130 sites, 100 occupied at that time) — the resort itself publishes no current lease terms, so any pad-rent or term figure quoted today is not verified until the resort states it.

Aquadel Crossing answers to two civic numbers in public sources. The developer address is 1885 Columbia Valley Rd while a current listing records the community at 1880 Columbia Valley Road — a small conflict that matters for title searches, locator runs and showing directions, and one to settle from the strata plan rather than from either marketing source. Property taxes — RURAL regime (Electoral Area H): properties pay FVRD and provincial rural taxes plus service-area levies (e.g., sewer where in the service area); the specific levy set for a given lot is not verified. Under the Taxation (Rural Area) Act, rural taxes are due and payable on July 2 of the year levied, with a 5% penalty on amounts unpaid on July 2 and a further 5% penalty on amounts unpaid on October 31 (s.11 regime).
Strata block (bare-land strata lots — the form of the three Lindell Beach communities): A fee-simple lot carries none of this.
Pad tenure (manufactured homes on rented pads — Lindell Beach Holiday Resort; Cultus Lake Village park): a manufactured home on a rented pad is NOT lot stock and NOT land ownership.

blocks.text: Good to know about Cultus Lake South

items.t: The south shore is the freehold shore (Nov 1, 2026). One road in, one road out (May 14, 2025). The FVRD's Area H update with emergency and evacuation plans records that Columbia Valley Road/Highway provides the populated area's only access, north to the Sardis and Yarrow exits of Highway 1 — the single-road reality drives emergency planning and summer traffic at the south end.

The year-round campground and the horse trail are at this end (Nov 1, 2026). Delta Grove Campground, in Cultus Lake Provincial Park at the southeast end of the lake, is the provincial park campground operating year-round, and the Watt Creek trailhead at the south end of the park is where the 20 km Cultus Lake Horse Trail from Edmeston Road ends.

Soowahlie First Nation (IR 14) is shown at the south end (Nov 1, 2026). The PlanCultus plan map shows Soowahlie First Nation (IR 14) at the south end of the lake — neighbouring jurisdiction a land buyer at the south shore should know exists on the plan map.

In the strata cottage communities, confirm what the strata owns versus what sits on the lot (Nov 1, 2026). The Province's strata buying guidance — review bylaws, rules, fees and any special levies, and confirm what the strata owns versus what sits on the lot — is the diligence frame the research itself gives for Creekside Mills, The Cottages and Aquadel Crossing.
